idiom_name: case/in on the discriminator plus a Hash registry of lambdas, Hash#transform_keys to the canonical shape
implementation_notes: Ruby's own tools make Translator objects unnecessary: case raw in {type: "csv", **rest} / in {type: "xml", **rest} (pattern matching, Ruby 3+) routes on the discriminator and binds the payload in one step, and a frozen Hash of lambdas keyed by the wire tag gives the same registry without a class hierarchy; Hash#transform_keys, #slice and #dig build the canonical hash, so the whole normalizer is a module of pure functions. Objects and deconstruct_keys stay justified when a translator carries state (a client for code lookups, per-partner configuration) or when matching should be expressed on domain objects rather than hashes, and a hand-written parser replaces JSON.parse for CSV or fixed-width sources.
code_sketch:
NORMALIZERS = {
  'csv'    => ->(p) { { id: p[:ref], amount_cents: to_cents(p[:amount]), currency: 'EUR' } },
  'legacy' => ->(p) { { id: p[:ID], amount_cents: p[:AMOUNT], currency: p[:CCY] || 'EUR' } },
}.freeze
def normalize(raw)
  body = JSON.parse(raw, symbolize_names: true)          # one key convention, at the seam
  case body
  in { type: String => type, payload: Hash => payload }  # routes and binds together
    NORMALIZERS.fetch(type).call(payload)                # KeyError, not a silent nil
  else
    raise UnknownWireFormat, body.inspect                # invalid-message channel
  end
end
pitfalls: Symbol versus string keys is the classic bug: JSON.parse returns string keys unless symbolize_names: true, and a mismatch turns every dig or pattern into a no-match that looks like 'field absent'.
Hash#dig returns nil both for a missing key and for an explicit JSON null, so it cannot distinguish absent from null - use key?/fetch when the canonical contract depends on the difference.
Pattern matching with **rest captures unknown keys into the canonical hash: filter with slice or explicit keys, or partner-controlled data ends up in the normalized message and in the logs.
Regex or split based CSV and date parsing accepts more than the contract (Date.parse guesses): parse with an explicit format and raise on failure.
